audit_findings.title: Temporary Section 45X credits may be capitalized into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $158.593m FY2026 benefit; $479.545m cumulative FY2024-FY2026; FY2026 benefit equals 54.7% of the $290m anchor; exact valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Section 45X reductions increase reported OE observations and therefore the trend anchor, explicit-period OE and terminal OE unless separately removed during the statutory phaseout.
audit_findings.evidence: The IRA includes multiple incentives to promote clean energy, and energy storage manufacturing among other provisions with tax credits available from 2023 to 2032, subject to phase out beginning in 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated forecast error: the supplied method perpetuates an anchor influenced by temporary credits but contains no explicit credit phaseout. The credits are large relative to anchor OE, and 49.7% of base operating value comes from the terminal value, so leaving the benefit in terminal economics can materially overstate value. The exact correction cannot be established without tracing the credits through taxes and each OE observation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct every OE observation excluding Section 45X benefits and the $25.037m prior-period estimate change, explicitly phase recurring credits out beginning in 2030, remove them entirely from terminal OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating or committed cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $530.663m bridge addition, equal to $13.95 per diluted share and 11.5% of the $4,606m base equity value; required operating cash and tax leakage unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash to operating value as a distributable nonoperating asset even though operations, capital projects and acquisitions may require that cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The majority of that cash and investments is expected to be utilized to fund local operating activities, capital expenditure requirements and acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that a substantial majority of cash is held abroad, considered indefinitely reinvested and expected to fund local activities. It therefore does not support treating the entire balance as excess. The precise correction remains unresolved because jurisdictional balances, minimum operating requirements, project commitments and repatriation leakage are not supplied, but the amount exposed is material to the per-share valuation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the jurisdictional cash schedule and committed-capital plan, determine minimum operating cash, quantify withholding and other repatriation taxes, and rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrably distributable without impairing forecast operations.

audit_findings.title: Derivative liabilities are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $71.6m gross liabilities and $0.7m assets at July 5, 2026; $70.883m net liability, equal to $1.86 per diluted share and 1.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any derivative obligation not offset by a hedged operating asset would be a non-debt claim deducted in the equity bridge; related settlements can also affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Those contracts that result in a liability position at March 31, 2026 are $73.8 million (pre-tax).
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, but a valuation error is unresolved because most of the balance comprises net-investment hedges that offset foreign operations already included in value. Even deducting the entire net liability with no offset would reduce base value only from $121.04 to about $119.18 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $181.91 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each derivative asset and liability to its hedged exposure and expected settlement, then deduct only unmatched claims; no full valuation rerun is needed unless that reconciliation identifies additional exposures.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pension obligations remain a senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.881m fiscal-2026 funded-status deficit, equal to $0.65 per diluted share and 0.54% of base equity value; fiscal-2027 expected contribution $1.621m
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded past-service obligation belongs in the equity bridge unless its required funding is already captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to make cash contributions of approximately $ 1,621 to its pension plans in fiscal 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The funded deficit is demonstrated, while possible double counting through pension expense remains unresolved. Even a conservative full bridge deduction would lower base value only to about $120.39 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $181.91 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the current funded status and settlement schedule, trace pension cash funding included in OE, and deduct only the portion not already captured.

audit_findings.title: Known restructuring costs extend beyond the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.7m aggregate originally estimated cash charges for Tijuana, Sao Paulo and Monterrey, equal to $1.04 per diluted share and 0.86% of base equity value; remaining amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecognized or unpaid one-time restructuring cash costs reduce near-term OE or require a separate equity-value deduction but should not reduce terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: EnerSys expects to incur a pre-tax charge of approximately $37 million under this restructuring plan when completed, the majority of which is expected to be incurred by the second half of fiscal year 2027, of which $14 million is expected to be non-cash charges primarily from accelerated depreciation.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that costs and cash outflows continue beyond fiscal 2026, while the valuation shows no transition adjustment. However, even charging the full original $39.7m cash estimates again—more than the remaining amount because portions have already been recognized—would not materially change the valuation conclusion. The exact remaining cash outflow is unresolved because recognized charges, accruals and payments are not fully reconciled and some estimates have evolved.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a plan-by-plan roll-forward of estimated cash costs, amounts expensed, accrued and paid through July 5, 2026; apply only the remaining undiscounted cash outflows as a transition adjustment and monitor estimate overruns.

audit_findings.title: European competition exposure is unreserved
audit_findings.mechanism: A fine, damages award or settlement would be a claim ahead of common equity; continuing customer losses or compliance costs could also reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, the Company did not have a reserve balance related to these matters.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated valuation error. Investigations and customer claims existed at the filing date, but no reserve, asserted-damages figure, estimable loss range or probable outcome is provided. The record therefore cannot establish materiality, while a sufficiently adverse resolution could affect value.
audit_findings.action: Review each subsequent filing and underlying legal disclosure for asserted damages, procedural developments, settlement discussions, insurance or indemnification, and any estimable loss range; rerun the bridge and OE only when a supportable exposure emerges.
